cards.hint: Think about the weaker pull described.
cards.quote: On the Moon g is about 1.62 m/s^2, roughly one sixth of the 9.8 m/s^2 we feel on Earth.
cards.stem: How does lunar gravity compare with the pull felt on Earth?

cards.hint: Think about what air would normally do.
cards.quote: On the Moon there is no air, so a thrown ball feels no drag at all.
cards.stem: What does a thrown ball feel during flight where there is no air?

cards.hint: Sideways motion has no push or pull.
options: stays U0 for the whole flight
cards.quote: Nothing pushes the ball sideways, so the horizontal speed stays U0 for the whole flight
cards.stem: What happens to horizontal speed after launch with no sideways push?

cards.hint: Look for the moment upward motion pauses.
cards.quote: The ball stops rising when V = 0, which happens at t = V0 / g.
cards.stem: When does the ball stop rising on the way up?
